title: GitHub documentation style guide (document-set level)
description: Secondary axis, retained for continuity with the published results. It is a document-set specification, not a general standard for code-level artifacts, so it is never used as the primary rubric.

criteria.name: Content Type Consistency
criteria.definition: Each article stays within a single content type rather than mixing types.
criteria.note: Document-set level specification; not a normative standard for docstrings.

criteria.name: Reuse Instead of Copying
criteria.definition: Existing content is reused by reference rather than duplicated.
criteria.note: Document-set level specification; not a normative standard for docstrings.

criteria.name: Balanced Hierarchy
criteria.definition: Headings form a balanced hierarchy without skipped or overloaded levels.
criteria.note: Document-set level specification; not a normative standard for docstrings.

criteria.name: Content Order
criteria.definition: Sections appear in the order a reader needs them.
criteria.note: Document-set level specification; not a normative standard for docstrings.

criteria.name: Category Title Naming
criteria.definition: Category titles use task-based gerunds and stay general and scalable.
criteria.note: Document-set level specification; not a normative standard for docstrings.

criteria.name: Title Standards
criteria.definition: Titles are clear, descriptive and concise, typically within 60-80 characters.
criteria.note: Document-set level specification; not a normative standard for docstrings.

criteria.name: Introduction Standards
criteria.definition: Introductions state what the article covers and who it is for.
criteria.note: Document-set level specification; not a normative standard for docstrings.

criteria.name: Permission Declaration Standards
criteria.definition: Permissions are stated upfront in the form 'People with [role] can [action].'
criteria.note: Document-set level specification; not a normative standard for docstrings.

criteria.name: Product Label Standards
criteria.definition: Product and feature names follow the documented label conventions.
criteria.note: Document-set level specification; not a normative standard for docstrings.

criteria.name: Process Content Standards
criteria.definition: Procedures are presented as clear step-by-step instructions.
criteria.note: Document-set level specification; not a normative standard for docstrings.

criteria.name: Next Steps Standards
criteria.definition: Follow-up links guide the reader to the next relevant topic.
criteria.note: Document-set level specification; not a normative standard for docstrings.

criteria.name: Further Reading Standards
criteria.definition: A bulleted list of external or advanced resources is provided.
criteria.note: Document-set level specification; not a normative standard for docstrings.

criteria.name: Prerequisites Standards
criteria.definition: Warnings and requirements are listed before sensitive tasks.
criteria.note: Document-set level specification; not a normative standard for docstrings.

criteria.name: Reference Content
criteria.definition: Reference information is presented as standalone articles or embedded sections.
criteria.note: Document-set level specification; not a normative standard for docstrings.

criteria.name: Conceptual Content Guidelines
criteria.definition: Conceptual topics begin with 'About [topic]' and explain purpose and use cases.
criteria.note: Document-set level specification; not a normative standard for docstrings.

criteria.name: Error Reference Content Guidelines
criteria.definition: Errors are documented so users can recognise and understand them, separately from troubleshooting.
criteria.note: Document-set level specification; not a normative standard for docstrings.

criteria.name: Tutorial Content Guidelines
criteria.definition: Tutorials define audience and goals and use a clear developer-oriented tone with examples.
criteria.note: Document-set level specification; not a normative standard for docstrings.

criteria.name: Getting Started Content Guidelines
criteria.definition: Quick starts are concise, step-based and ideally under 600 words.
criteria.note: Document-set level specification; not a normative standard for docstrings.
